title: Kyoto Attraction Finds Fun in 'Night Farming'
paragraphs: Kyoto is famous for its temples, gardens and traditional streets. But visitors can now try something very different there: picking vegetables on a farm at night.

The event is called Night Farm, and it is held by BNR Farm in Nishikyo Ward, in the west of Kyoto. In 2026, it was held from July 3 to November 3. It was closed on Wednesdays and Thursdays, and visitors had to make a reservation.

The fields are lit up with lights in the evening, and visitors pick vegetables in the dark. When the season is at its peak, they can pick up to about 20 kinds of Kyoto vegetables. These include several kinds of eggplant, cucumbers, okra, cherry tomatoes and local peppers. Then, visitors put the fresh vegetables on pizzas and cook them in a stone oven. They can also eat a seasonal vegetable dish and cook vegetables on a barbecue. At the end, they can take home vegetables worth about 2,000 yen.

The standard plan costs 6,050 yen for adults and 3,025 yen for elementary school children. There is also a more expensive plan, which costs 13,200 yen for adults. In this plan, a farmer helps visitors and gives them drinks and extra pizza toppings.

Night Farm started in 2025, and about 1,400 people came in three months. In 2026, the farm changed the activities every month. For example, in summer, visitors could try nagashi somen, where people catch cold noodles as they flow down a long tube with water.

The event is part of a trend in Japan to create more things for tourists to do at night. But while most night tourism happens in cities, Night Farm brings it to the countryside. Night Farm is also testing similar events in other parts of Kyoto Prefecture and in Nagano Prefecture.
